topic: White spot on a phone screen: LCD backlight pressure marks, stuck pixels and OLED image persistence
record_type: Draft on a branch; publishes to main only after owner approval in chat
uniqueness: 72-guide inventory checked. No white spot, bright spot or pressure-mark guide existed in tips/ or guides/. Nearest pages are lcd-vs-oled (screen type and pricing), cracked-screen-safe-to-use, iphone-green-white-line-screen and samsung-screen-issues, all linked. Queue item 4 from the owner's keyword list (4,900; iFixit ranks #4 with an Answers thread). The Acer Chromebook item was skipped on the owner's word.
scope: A white or bright spot that stays in one place on a phone display while the picture changes. Cracked glass, colored lines, black ink-like damage and white spots that appear only in photos are routed to other guides.

sources.retrieval: Read. OLED Super Retina models (iPhone X, XS, XS Max; iPhone 11 Pro models and later excluding iPhone SE 2nd and 3rd generation). Image persistence is temporary and fades after a few minutes of normal use; burn-in in extreme cases.
Read. iPhone 11 tech specs list an LCD Multi-Touch display with IPS technology.
Read. iPhone SE (2nd generation) tech specs list an LCD.
Read. iPhone SE (3rd generation) tech specs list an LCD.
Read. Stuck pixels stay lit in one color from an electrical fault; pressure and impact listed as causes; solid-color test, Safe mode check.
Read. LCD backlight layers: light guide plate, diffuser, reflector. OLED needs no backlight.
Read. Bright spots from external pressure, frame pressure and heat; no DIY fix.
Read. Repair chain post: cloudy patch on a white background on LCD; pressure from bags and tight clothing; resets do not repair physical damage. Cited as an example, not as proof.
Read. 2014 Answers thread: white spots after an LCD swap traced to a bent battery pressing from behind. Cited as an example.
Not readable: returned the Samsung support home page. Not cited.
Read in part (opening post and one reply). Not cited; iPhone XR display type not confirmed from an Apple page, so XR is not named.
